comparator.name: Fiscale Economie
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official programme and curriculum pages establish a three-year, 180-ECTS Dutch-language bachelor combining economics, business, law and taxation. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 compulsory ECTS. Year 3 contains a genuine 30-ECTS choice among exchange/study abroad, a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective, or Economics and Management minors; this open space is preserved rather than instantiated. The remaining 30 ECTS comprise four compulsory 6-ECTS courses and a 6-ECTS bachelor thesis. The table displays the thesis under both semesters because it may start in either semester, while explicitly stating that its total load is 6 ECTS; it is therefore counted once. Zero-credit GROW activities are programme features but are excluded from the 180-ECTS component total. No formal route is selected.

Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme’s combined fiscal-economics identity, general tax-policy and legislation interests, major tax bases, effects on economic choices, and relationship between economic developments and tax law. Two further generator-backed clusters remain: corporate and multinational taxation with financial/legal analysis supports a business, accounting and finance direction; tax justice, societal tax questions, beneficial fiscal policy and perspective-balancing support a public-policy and social-equity direction. Both are coherent, mechanically feasible and materially distinct while explicitly acknowledging that UCR offers no specialist Dutch tax curriculum. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses, while the two related directions differ by eleven; all three alternatives are included.

Compulsory bachelor thesis; students start in semester 1 or semester 2, for a total of 6 ECTS.

notes.text: Tilburg’s programme is a specialist fiscal-economics degree combining a continuous sequence in Dutch personal, business, corporate and value-added taxation with economics, accounting, finance, public and private law, European and international tax, formal tax procedure, ethics and a fiscal-economics thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with business, accounting, finance, broad law, politics, sociology and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, personal and corporate income tax, VAT, formal tax procedure or the programme’s multi-course fiscal sequence. These pathways therefore compare related economic, business, legal and policy fields; none reproduces the external fiscal-economics discipline or its professional preparation.
